fix.digest: Clendon was present to witness the first signatures at Waitangi. As consul of a rival power he had a direct interest in what Britain was acquiring and how firmly.

fix.digest: Clendon wrote to Shortland asking to be furnished with a copy of any treaty made with the chiefs, to send to the United States government. A note of 6 April records that he was to receive a copy and a translation.

problem: Labilliere prints the 23 October 1835 letter. In it Batman says he proposed to move to Port Phillip with his family, asks Arthur to inform Bourke of the Association's plans, complains of settlers ignoring the treaty and asks for authority to control them, and reports 80 to 100 Aboriginal people fed and clothed. The digest did not report its contents and mixed in the tribute claim, which rests on Knapman alone.

fix.digest: Batman wrote to Arthur that, now the New South Wales governor claimed jurisdiction, he hoped Arthur would tell Bourke of the Association's plans. He complained of men settling on the land without regard to the treaty, asked for authority to control settlers, reported eighty to a hundred Aboriginal people being fed and clothed, and said he meant to move to Port Phillip with his family at once.
fix.quote: I propose immediately to proceed with my family to Port Phillip
fix.source_note: Batman to Arthur, Launceston, 23 October 1835, in Labilliere (1878).

problem: Gellibrand's 'kindness and conciliation' remark is about Buckley's own nervous, irritable temperament ('he can only be acted upon by kindness and conciliation'), not Buckley's view of the people.

text_replace.old: He recorded Buckley's view that the people could only be moved by kindness and conciliation.
text_replace.new: He judged Buckley nervous and easily annoyed, which he put down to his long isolation, and concluded that Buckley himself could only be handled with kindness.

problem: This rests only on a Wikipedia mirror. The State Library Victoria timeline has Wedge leading the Indented Head party to the Yarra on 2 September 1835 and finding the Fawkner party already there. Labilliere does not describe Wedge telling them of the purchase.

fix.digest: Wedge led the men from the Indented Head camp to the Yarra and found Fawkner's party already settled on the site. Later accounts say the Association's men told them the land had been bought from the chiefs; Fawkner's party stayed, and Fawkner treated the deed as worthless.
fix.source_note: SLV, Victoria's early colonial history timeline (Wedge, 2 September 1835); the warning to Fawkner's men rests on secondary summaries only.

fix.digest: Fawkner's manuscript journal closes on 8 August 1836, a year after his party first reached the Yarra; the published edition (Billot, 1982) is the place to read its entries.

text_replace.new: Todd's journal opens on 8 June, as Batman prepared to leave the small party at Indented Head, and runs to 15 November 1835: the daily record of a camp in contact with Wadawurrung (Wathaurong) people.

problem: Bonwick's narrative says the Rebecca 'was forced on Tuesday to put into Port Sorell'. Tuesday was 19 May 1835, not Wednesday 20 May.
